newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil foreign direct investment seen at $7.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil foreign direct investment seen at $7.5 bln.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank expects net foreign direct investment to total at least $7.5 billion this year, compared with $3.928 billion in 1995, said Altamir Lopes, head of the bank's economics department.
For the first 10 months of 1996, foreign direct investment totalled $6.638 billion, against $2.939 in the same 1995 period.
"If the pace continues like this, foreign direct investment should end 1996 at at least $7.5 billion," Lopes said.
Some government officials have predicted net foreign direct investment of $8.0-9.0 billion for the year.
